intro.title: Unnecessary Re-renders
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular counter application to understand and fix unnecessary re-renders. You will learn how Angular's change detection can cause components to re-render even when their data hasn't changed, which can hurt performance. The core concept involves using Angular's OnPush change detection strategy and pure pipes to control when updates occur. You'll work with components, templates, and lifecycle hooks to optimize your app.
intro.usecase: Unnecessary re-renders are a critical performance concern in real-world Angular applications, especially in data-intensive interfaces like financial dashboards or e-commerce product filters. For example, updating a single stock price in a live dashboard shouldn't cause the entire chart and table to re-render, as this would degrade the user experience with lag and high CPU usage. Similarly, in a large form with dependent fields, changing one input should not trigger re-evaluation of every other field's validation logic. By mastering techniques to prevent these wasteful updates, developers ensure their applications remain responsive and scalable under real user loads.
